bottleneck: Batched prompt admission can upload experts and evict decode residents even when the next single-token request has a different working set. R42 observed prompt churn. R51 already bypassed oversized batches, so this option has no assumed benefit on those cells.
hypothesis: On RDNA2/RADV, bypassing pool admission for MoE ID tensors with more than one token can avoid pool uploads, remap allocation and cache pollution while keeping the existing expert-copy fallback. This does not remove all prompt transfers or routing readbacks.
option: GGML_SCHED_EXPERT_POOL_DECODE_ONLY; absent=original behavior, present (including0)=bypass admission when ids.ne[1]>1. Single-token prompt chunks can still admit. Batched decode/speculation also bypasses; this is a shape rule, not a semantic phase detector.
minimal_change: One opt-in member and early admission return in scheduler expert pool; reuse current fallback and graph restoration. Existing multilayer fixture injects cache-admission abort only on shapes eligible for admission, and still checks all batched output vectors.
tradeoffs: Cold TG can upload more after PP; batching or concurrency can bypass useful cache hits. Existing resident payload stays allocated. No claimed VRAM saving or faster end-to-end generation before measurement.
